ui.purpose: Buttons, labels, tabs, chrome — the bulk of the interface.

machine.purpose: Code, diffs, paths, ids, ticking figures — earned monospace only.

shadows.name: elevation-hairline
shadows.purpose: The only depth cue a flat card or panel gets.

shadows.name: dialog
shadows.purpose: Modal overlays only — the one tier granted a real shadow.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default easing for entrances and toggles.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The trace-green solid action button (Send, Approve).
components.css: .ds-btn-solid { background: #3FBFB4; color: #0E1013; font-weight: 500; font-size: 12.5px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', sans-serif; padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 3px; border: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-solid:hover { background: #57D6CB; } .ds-btn-solid:focus-visible { outline: 1px solid #3FBFB4; } .ds-btn-solid:disabled { opacity: 0.45; cursor: default; }

components.name: Armed Button
components.description: Amber confirmation-step button for a high-risk action.
components.css: .ds-btn-armed { background: #E0A458; color: #14161A; font-weight: 500; font-size: 12.5px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', sans-serif; padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 3px; border: none; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-armed:hover { background: #E9B872; }

components.name: Outline Button
components.description: Transparent bordered button; hover reddens toward a destructive action.
components.css: .ds-btn-outline { background: transparent; color: #9AA2AC; border: 1px solid rgba(221, 225, 230, 0.3); font-size: 12.5px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', sans-serif; padding: 6px 14px; border-radius: 3px; cursor: pointer; } .ds-btn-outline:hover { border-color: rgba(224, 104, 94, 0.5); color: #E0685E; }

components.name: Risk Chip
components.description: Low/medium/high/plan risk label on an inbox card.
components.css: .ds-chip-risk { font-size: 11px; border-radius: 3px; padding: 1px 6px; white-space: nowrap; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', sans-serif; } .ds-chip-risk--high { color: #E0685E; border: 1px solid rgba(224, 104, 94, 0.45); background: rgba(224, 104, 94, 0.07); }

components.name: Marker Chip
components.description: Approved/denied/pending/expired marker on a stream event.
components.css: .ds-chip-marker { border-radius: 3px; padding: 1px 7px; font-size: 11px; white-space: nowrap; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', sans-serif; } .ds-chip-marker--pending { color: #E0A458; border: 1px solid rgba(224, 164, 88, 0.4); background: rgba(224, 164, 88, 0.07); }

components.name: Field / Composer Input
components.description: Multi-line composer field with a block caret and earned monospace.
components.css: .ds-input { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, 'Cascadia Mono', Consolas, monospace; font-size: 13px; color: #DDE1E6; background: #0E1013; border: 1px solid rgba(221, 225, 230, 0.3); border-radius: 3px; padding: 6px 10px; caret-shape: block; caret-color: #3FBFB4; } .ds-input:focus { outline: 1px solid #3FBFB4; }

components.name: Card
components.description: The base panel/card surface: flat, hairline-bordered, no shadow.
components.css: .ds-card { background: #1A1D22; border: 1px solid rgba(221, 225, 230, 0.16); border-radius: 3px; padding: 10px 13px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(221, 225, 230, 0.06); }

components.name: Sidebar Row (selected)
components.description: Project sidebar row with the carry-over 2px inset selection mark, recorded as a defect, not a rule to copy.
components.css: .ds-sidebar-row { font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', 'Inter', sans-serif; font-size: 12.5px; color: #DDE1E6; padding: 6px 10px; } .ds-sidebar-row--sel { background: rgba(221, 225, 230, 0.1); box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 #3FBFB4; }

narrative.overview:
The Trace is an instrument screen, not a console and not a dashboard. It refuses the console-with-one-neon-accent register and the white-card-dashboard register alike, and it refuses its own predecessor, The Sixteen-Colour Field, an indexed sixteen-ink palette with a bitmap face that could not render below 12px and cost the board its density on a populated screen. The ground is neutral charcoal, ruled by a faint graticule of hairline borders; the interface is otherwise monochrome, and the one accent colour marks the live trace. Every other colour that appears is a reading outside tolerance, never decoration.

The build is dense by requirement, not by style preference: PRODUCT.md fixes information density as a structural constraint, because the application is watched for hours with several sessions in flight, and it must hold six lanes, a branch, a filesystem path, a timer and a count on one row without truncating. That is the exact fault that killed the previous world, so this one returns to an 11px floor on a system typeface with real weights, rather than a display face with a legibility floor.

PRODUCT.md's Brand Commitments state plainly that no visual register is binding: palette, typeface, corner geometry, rule weight, density and elevation are all replaceable, and this record describes the current build, not a locked identity. Two prior worlds, The Engraved Score and The Deployable Sheet, and the sixteen-ink world named above, are rejected and stand only as anti-reference; nothing from them survives in the build and nothing here should be read as reviving them.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral charcoal ground (never navy, never pure black) under a faint hairline graticule.
One accent, a teal-green trace colour, reserved for action and running state.
Every other colour is earned by being out of tolerance: amber for attention owed, red for error.
A system UI typeface throughout, 11-20px; monospace reserved for machine text where the character grid carries meaning.
Materials are flat: a hairline lip for depth, no gradients, no glows, no bevels.

rules.name: The Tolerance Rule
rules.body: Colour is spent solely on a measurement outside tolerance. A board with nothing wrong is monochrome except for the one live trace; amber and red are earned by an actual reading, never applied for emphasis or decoration.

rules.name: The Fine Gets No Hue Rule
rules.body: A finished lane draws no colour, so it cannot compete for attention with a lane that still needs the developer. `.pill.done` is neutral ink, not green, even though green is otherwise the "good" colour elsewhere in the system.

rules.name: The Identity-Never-State Rule
rules.body: Teal and purple identify a surface (e.g. a database connection); they never report status. Status colours are exactly trace-green, amber and red.

rules.name: The Monospace Is Earned Rule
rules.body: `.mono`/`.code` are applied only where the character grid carries meaning: code, commands, paths, ids, diffs, and figures that tick. Labels, names, statuses, buttons and tabs are interface chrome and are set in the UI face.

rules.name: The Legible-At-Density Rule
rules.body: No type tier may require a face with a legibility floor above roughly 11px. A type system that forces a larger floor to stay legible is disqualified regardless of how it reads on an empty screen.

rules.name: The Earned Shadow Rule
rules.body: A real, blurred box-shadow is granted only to the overlay tier (dialogs, dropdowns, menus). Every other surface is flat with, at most, the elevation hairline.

rules.name: No Glow Rule
rules.body: A coloured shadow is elevation, and elevation says "this is the one thing to do here." It is reserved for the composer's Send button and nothing else.

dos: Do reserve colour for a reading outside tolerance: trace-green for action/running, amber for attention owed, red for error. A monochrome board is the correct default state.
Do set every label, button, tab and status string in the system UI face; reserve monospace for code, paths, ids, diffs and ticking figures.
Do keep shadows flat except at the overlay tier (dialog, dropdown, menu), and always pair an offset with a blur when a shadow is used.
Do hold identity colours (teal, purple) clear of the status colours (green, amber, red) so an identity marker can never be misread as a state.
donts: Don't add a gradient, a gloss layer, or a coloured glow to any button or panel. `--gloss` and `--green-glow` are both `none` throughout the build.

Don't revive the sixteen-ink indexed palette, the DotGothic16 bitmap face, ordered dither, hard block shadows, bevelled edges, 0px card radii, or a 12px+ type floor. That world was built and explicitly rejected; PRODUCT.md records it as anti-reference, not as a style to draw from.

Don't treat a 2px coloured border-left/inset rule as a system pattern for "selected." It appears on a few rows as a carried-over defect from an earlier world, not as an established selection idiom; the craft floor for this world holds selection marks to 1px.
Don't promise a drawn measurement graticule or per-lane stepping traces as shipped behaviour. Neither is built; both remain plain hairline borders and static rows respectively.
